title: the system-header writer was given a constant size instead of the space actually left
object: the muxer's output buffer, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a bit writer initialised with a constant capacity rather than the remaining space
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation, no inner layer.
fidelity: model consumer, real constant: 128 is upstream's hardcoded value, and the case asserts that the remaining space is smaller than it.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavformat/mpegenc.c passes a buffer size into put_system_header and calls `init_put_bits(&pb, buf, buf_size)`. The pre-fix form, `init_put_bits(&pb, buf, 128)` with no size parameter, is at b2df2f4f22^.

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **CAUGHT** at ffh_write_probe_u8+0x58 -- cause 7, a bounds violation on a store; pc=0xc020eb78, address=0xc02521c0.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc020e5b8 address=0xc0251768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image 1e801599dd54e698. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x10221a, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x102202` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

native-detect.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at the labelled probe on the buggy arm and is silent on the fixed arm -- keyed on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string AddressSanitizer.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions. Capstone measured 2026-10-09 (results/2026-10-09-capstone/): spatial CAUGHT, sublet CAUGHT.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner allocator between, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the crossing comes from a CONSTANT capacity rather than a computed one, so it appears only when the writer is called with a cursor far enough into the buffer -- the defect is in what the callee was told, not in what it wrote.
